Like other texts in the Apadāna collection, it presents the biographical verses of a Buddhist elder (thera), commemorating a past act of generosity—the offering of *isimugga* beans or pulses—and recounting the resultant karmic fruits and spiritual attainment [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the poem across five different languages [SuttaCentral].
